context: Two elders reminisce about youthful religious customs
purpose: Teach: 礼拝/葬儀/福音/民衆/講じ/クリスチャン/詩人/規範

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 幼い頃、日曜礼拝に祖母と通ったのを今でもよく覚えていますよ。
lines.en: I still vividly remember going to Sunday worship with my grandmother as a young child.
lines.style: Soft nostalgic tone, slow pacing, gentle warmth in voice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: ああ、うちの村にも敬虔なクリスチャン家庭が何軒かあってね、葬儀社よりも教会で見送る方が多かったのよ。
lines.en: Ah, our village had several devout Christian families too — more farewells happened at the church than through funeral homes.
lines.style: Warm reminiscing grandmother, soft trailing sentences, slight wistful sigh.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 牧師さんが福音書を朗読してくださって、まるで詩人の言葉のように響いたものです。
lines.en: The pastor would read from the Gospel, and his voice resonated like the words of a poet.
lines.style: Reverent, slow recall, hushed admiration in delivery.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: ええ、当時は民衆の暮らしの中に、そういう静かな規範が自然と根付いていましたねえ。
lines.en: Yes, back then a quiet moral code was naturally rooted in the everyday lives of ordinary people.
lines.style: Reflective grandmother cadence, drawn-out sentence endings, gentle nodding feel.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い牧師が公民館で道徳を講じてくれた夜もあって、子どもながらに胸が熱くなりました。
lines.en: There were also evenings when a young pastor lectured on morality at the community hall — even as a child, it stirred my heart.
lines.style: Gentle reminiscence, slight emotional weight, careful elder phrasing.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 今の若い人たちには、ちょっと想像しにくい世界かもしれませんねえ。
lines.en: It might be a world that's a little hard for today's young people to even imagine.
lines.style: Soft chuckle, affectionate concern, gentle elder warmth.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうですね、ですが、ああいう時間がなければ、私という人間はできていなかった気がします。
lines.en: Indeed — and yet, without those moments, I don't think I would have become the person I am.
lines.style: Heartfelt closing reflection, slow tempo, quiet conviction.
